extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for petitions/requests to advance examination (make an application special), including accelerated and prioritized examination pathways and the documentary, claim‑limit, search, and interview requirements to participate. Covers grounds (health, age, environment, energy, counter‑terrorism), handling, and procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement of examination general rule (37 CFR 1.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be advanced out of turn for examination or further action except as provided by this part, upon order of the Director, upon filing of a request under paragraph (b) or (e), or upon filing a petition or request under paragraph (c) or (d) with a showing which, in the opinion of the Director, will justify so advancing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching limitation: only the statutory/regulatory grounds or Director orders permit advancement. Petitions/requests must demonstrate justification; see specific paragraphs for eligible bases and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance for inventions of peculiar importance upon government request (37 CFR 1.102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications wherein the inventions are deemed of peculiar importance to some branch of the public service and the head of some department of the Government requests immediate action may be advanced for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such advancement requires a department head's request and Director order; treated as special cases (see special cases list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special without fee for applicant's age or health (37 CFR 1.102(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make an application special may be filed without a fee if the basis is the applicant’s age or health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subsections I and II for evidentiary requirements (e.g., doctor's certificate for health; statement or registered practitioner evidence for age ≥65). Personal/medical info submitted becomes public unless submitted under MPEP §724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special without fee for inventions materially enhancing environment/energy/countering terrorism (37 CFR 1.102(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make an application special may be filed without a fee if the invention will materially (i) enhance the quality of the environment, (ii) contribute to the development or conservation of energy resources, or (iii) contribute to countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must state the basis; if disclosure doesn't make materiality clear, include an explanatory statement under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how the materiality standard is met. The materiality standard disallows mere speculation or reliance on minor aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee required for petitions on other grounds (37 CFR 1.102(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make an application special on grounds other than those referred to in paragraph (c) must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not qualifying under the no‑fee grounds (age, health, env/energy/terrorism, PPH), the petitioner must pay the statutory fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination filing requirements and claim limits (37 CFR 1.102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination must comply with the paragraph’s requirements and be accompanied by prioritized examination fee (§1.17(c)), processing fee (§1.17(i)), and if not already paid, the publication fee (§1.18(d)). An application for prioritized examination may not contain or be amended to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or any multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritized examination is limited by application type (see exclusions) and annual cap (no more than 15,000 requests per fiscal year). Must also meet the specific filing/timing requirements in e(1) or e(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination exclusions and annual cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritized examination will not be accorded to international applications not entered into national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, design applications, reissue applications, provisional applications, or reexamination proceedings. No more than 15,000 requests will be accepted in any fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check application type eligibility and yearly capacity before requesting prioritized examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination with original nonprovisional application (e)(1) filing content/time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination may be filed with an original utility or plant nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a). The application must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including at least one claim, a drawing when necessary, and the inventor’s oath or declaration on filing (though the oath/declaration may be postponed per §1.53(f)(3) if an ADS meeting conditions is present). Utility applications must be filed via USPTO patent electronic filing system and include filing, search, and examination fees upon filing; plant applications must include their applicable fees. The request must be present upon filing, except applicant may file an amendment to cancel any independent claims in excess of four, any total claims in excess of thirty, and any multiple dependent claim not later than one month from a first decision on the request; this one‑month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict completeness and fee requirements at filing. The one‑month cure period is non‑extendable; ensure claim counts comply or be prepared to timely amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination with RCE (e)(2) timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination may be filed with or after a request for continued examination (RCE) under §1.114. For utility applications the request must be filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system before the mailing of the first Office action after the RCE. Only a single such request may be granted in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is critical—file prior to the first OA after the RCE; only one RCE‑based prioritized request permitted per application.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of special cases that are advanced out of turn (MPEP list A–J)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual enumerates categories of special cases that are advanced out of turn, including (A) inventions of peculiar public‑service importance upon government request, (B) applications made special via petition/prioritized exam/PPH, (C) reissue applications (esp. in stayed litigation), (D) applications remanded by an appellate tribunal, (E) applications taken up by earliest claimed domestic benefit date and transferred, (F) applications appearing to interfere with other applications or unexpired patents, (G) applications ready for allowance (or almost ready), (H) applications in condition for final rejection, (I) applications pending more than 5 years (including effective pendency >5 years), and (J) reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories guide examiner/TC priority handling; check the particular category applicability and cited MPEP / CFR references for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal/medical evidence public availability and alternative submission (health/age petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal/medical information submitted as evidence to support a health or age petition will be available to the public if the application file is available to the public under 37 CFR 1.11 or 1.14. If the applicant does not wish this information to become part of the application file, the information must be submitted pursuant to MPEP §724.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider filing sensitive evidence under the separate procedures specified in MPEP §724.02 to avoid public disclosure of personal/medical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant’s health petition evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon a petition by applicant accompanied by any evidence showing the state of health of the inventor or joint inventor is such that they might not be available to assist in prosecution if the application ran its normal course (e.g., a doctor’s certificate or other medical certificate). No fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence should establish likely unavailability; the statement must be made in good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant’s age petition evidentiary standard (65+)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon filing a petition including evidence showing the inventor or joint inventor is 65 years of age or more (e.g., a statement by the inventor or a statement from a registered practitioner that they have evidence of age). No fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentary or practitioner‑attested evidence of age; same public‑availability caveat as health petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental quality materiality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions which materially enhance the quality of the environment of mankind by contributing to the restoration or maintenance of the basic life‑sustaining natural elements (air, water, soil). The petition must state special status is sought for this reason. No fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure does not on its face show material enhancement, the petition must include an explanatory statement showing how the materiality standard is met. Speculation about hypothetical end‑user uses or minor aspects is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy contribution materiality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions which materially contribute to (A) discovery/development of energy resources or (B) more efficient utilization and conservation of energy resources. Petition must state the category. No fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (fossil fuels, hydrogen, nuclear, solar; energy efficiency in combustion systems, appliances). If disclosure is not clear, petition must include explanatory statement. Speculation or minor aspects are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Countering terrorism materiality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions which materially contribute to countering terrorism. Petition must state special status is sought for this reason. No fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International terrorism definition cited (18 U.S.C. 2331); example technologies listed (detection/identification sensors, security systems, barricades/disabling systems, explosives/vehicular systems). If disclosure is not clear, petition must include explanatory statement; speculative/minor aspects do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions and decisions recorded in application file; deciding office
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition to make special or request to advance examination, regardless of ground and nature of decision, is made of record in the application file, together with the decision thereon. Petitions (with attachments/supporting affidavits) are provided as a single document in the file wrapper and the decision as a separate document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently petitions based on health/age, PPH participation, pilot programs, and requests for prioritized examination under 1.102(e) are decided by the Office of Petitions. All other petitions to make special are decided by the Quality Assurance Specialist of the Technology Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination eligibility (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted accelerated examination status only if it meets the conditions in subsection I (the accelerated examination program requirements). Petitions to make special filed on/after Aug 25, 2006 must meet these revised requirements (except health/age/PPH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the listed items (A–I) below for the detailed filing, claim, search, support‑document, and interview obligations for accelerated examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement A: petition form and fee or qualifying statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be filed with a petition to make special under the accelerated examination program accompanied by either the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h) or a statement that the claimed subject matter is directed to environmental quality, the development/conservation of energy resources, or countering terrorism. Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed form and include the correct fee or qualifying materiality statement; failing this will prevent grant of accelerated status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement B: application type (non‑reissue utility or design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be a non‑reissue utility or design application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue applications are excluded from accelerated examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement C: electronic filing and contingency for system unavailability
rubrics_metrics.description: The application, petition, and required fees must be filed electronically using the USPTO patent electronic filing system. If the system is not available during normal business hours, applicant may file by mail accompanied by a statement that the system was not available. Applicant should prominently indicate the paper filing is under the accelerated examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper filing due to EFS outage may delay final disposition beyond the 12‑month goal; clearly mark the filing to aid processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement D: application must be complete under 37 CFR 1.51 and in condition for examination at time of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing, the application must be complete under 37 CFR 1.51 and in condition for examination — filed with basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, application size fee (if applicable), and an executed inventor’s oath or declaration for each inventor (required for entry into program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting an oath/declaration after filing would delay processing and hamper meeting the 12‑month goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement E: strict claim limits and appeal behavior agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain three or fewer independent claims and twenty or fewer total claims, and must not contain any multiple dependent claims. By filing the petition the applicant agrees not to separately argue the patentability of any dependent claim during any appeal in the application (dependent claims will be grouped with the parent independent claim). The petition must include a statement consenting to this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a binding procedural concession — include the required statement (form PTO/SB/28) and ensure claim counts comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement F: single‑invention requirement and election without traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must be directed to a single invention. If the USPTO determines claims are not directed to a single invention, applicant must make an election without traverse in a telephonic interview. The petition must include a statement that applicant will agree to make such an election without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant refuses or cannot be reached, claim 1 may be constructively elected without traverse; ensure claim set unity or be prepared to elect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement G: interview agreement (including pre‑first OA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must be willing to have an interview (including an interview before a first Office action) to discuss the prior art and potential rejections or objections with the intention of clarifying and possibly resolving issues with respect to patentability. The petition must include a statement agreeing to have such an interview when requested by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO will generally not issue an Office action rejecting claims before attempting an interview; be prepared to engage in examiner conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement H: preexamination search statement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing, applicant must provide a statement that a preexamination search was conducted, including identification of the field of search by CPC group/subgroup (or US class/subclass for designs) and the date of the search. For database searches, provide the search logic or chemical structure/sequence used as a query, the name of the files searched and the database service, and the date of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough, well‑documented preexamination search is required and must be tied to the claimed invention; insufficient or undocumented searches can cause denial of accelerated status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preexamination search scope requirement H(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preexamination search must involve U.S. patents and patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and non‑patent literature, unless the applicant can justify with reasonable certainty that no references more pertinent than those already identified are likely to be found in any eliminated source and includes such justification with the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit categories of prior art without a careful, documented justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preexamination search claim‑coverage requirement H(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preexamination search must be directed to the claimed invention and encompass all of the features of the claims, giving the claims the broadest reasonable interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search must match the BRIEST reasonable reading of the claims and cover all claim elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preexamination search coverage of disclosed features H(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preexamination search must also encompass disclosed features that may be claimed. An amendment to the claims not encompassed by the preexamination search or an updated accelerated examination support document will be treated as not fully responsive and will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subsequent claim amendments require an updated search/document that covers the new claim scope at time of filing; otherwise the amendment will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign search reports generally insufficient H(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A search report from a foreign patent office will not satisfy the preexamination search requirement unless the search report itself satisfies the preexamination search requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on foreign office search reports unless they meet the detailed content/scope requirements described for preexamination searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good faith requirement for search statement H(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement in support of a petition to make special must be based on a good faith belief that the preexamination search was conducted in compliance with these requirements (see 37 CFR 1.56 and 11.18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements must be truthful and made with the duty of candor in mind; false or non‑good‑faith statements can have sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination support document required (I) — IDS inclusion I(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing, applicant must provide an accelerated examination support document that includes an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.98 citing each reference deemed most closely related to the subject matter of each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and disclose the most relevant references up front; the support document is central to accelerated prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support document: mapping claim limitations to references I(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each reference cited, the support document must identify all the limitations in the claims that are disclosed by the reference specifying where the limitation is disclosed in the cited reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise claim‑to‑reference mappings (citations to specific pages/cols/lines/figs) to show where each claim element appears in the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support document: detailed patentability explanation I(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The support document must include a detailed explanation of how each of the claims are patentable over the references cited with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide claim‑by‑claim, element‑by‑element arguments explaining patentability over the cited art with the required particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support document: concise statement of utility I(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The support document must include a concise statement of the utility of the invention as defined in each of the independent claims (unless the application is a design application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the practical utility tied to the claimed subject matter for each independent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support document: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) written‑description support showing I(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The support document must include a showing of where each limitation of the claims finds support under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (or first paragraph pre‑AIA 112) in the written description of the specification. If applicable, identify each means‑/step‑plus‑function element invoking 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and the corresponding structure, material, or acts in the specification. If claiming benefit to earlier applications, include where each limitation finds support in each such application where support exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise citations to the specification (and any priority documents) showing written‑description support for each claim limitation, and identify structure for means‑plus‑function elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support document: AIA/pre‑AIA prior‑art status identification I(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) For AIA applications subject to first‑to‑file, the support document must identify any cited references that disclose subject matter that may be excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). (ii) For pre‑AIA (first‑to‑invent) applications, the support document must identify any cited references that may be disqualified as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) as amended by the CREATE Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag references that may be statutorily excluded/disqualified under the applicable statutory regime and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on petition: notification, single opportunity to perfect, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application/petition does not meet all requirements for special status (including insufficient search), applicant will be notified of defects and the application will remain in regular status. Where the petition/support document is defective in one or more requirements, applicant will be given a single opportunity to perfect the petition or support document within two months. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are permitted, but filing a petition for extension will result in the application being taken out of the accelerated examination program. This opportunity does not apply to applications not in condition for examination on filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely perfection can lead to grant but final disposition may occur later than 12 months. Be careful with extension petitions — they remove accelerated status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examiner action timing and telephone interview restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Once granted special status, the application will be docketed and taken up expeditiously (e.g., within two weeks). If claims are not directed to a single invention, the telephone restriction practice (MPEP §812.01) will apply and applicant must make an election without traverse during the telephonic interview. If the applicant refuses to elect or cannot be reached, the examiner will treat claim 1 as constructively elected without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect prompt examiner contact and be prepared for telephonic election without traverse if unity issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interview and Office action issuance policy for accelerated exam
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO determines a possible rejection or other issue must be addressed, the examiner will telephone the applicant to discuss the issue and any possible amendment or submission to resolve it. The USPTO will not issue an Office action (other than a notice of allowance) unless either (A) an interview was conducted but did not place the application in condition for allowance, or (B) there is a determination that an interview is unlikely to result in allowance. Prior to mailing any Office action rejecting the claims, the USPTO will conduct a conference to review the rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners will use interviews and internal conferences to try to resolve issues before issuing rejecting OAs; applicants should be ready to participate in interviews promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory response period for OAs and extension consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action other than a notice of allowance is mailed, the Office action will set a shortened statutory period of two months. Extensions of this shortened period under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are permitted, but filing a petition for extension will result in the application being taken out of the accelerated examination program. Failure to timely file a reply will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to respond within the shortened two‑month window or accept removal from the program if seeking extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply scope limitations and treatment of non‑responsive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to an Office action must be limited to the rejections, objections, and requirements made. Any amendment that attempts to (A) add claims resulting in >3 independent or >20 total claims, (B) present claims not encompassed by the preexamination search or updated support document, or (C) present claims directed to a nonelected invention or an invention other than previously claimed, will be treated as not fully responsive and will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments stay within claim limits and are encompassed by the original (or updated) search/support doc; otherwise they will be rejected as non‑responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file updated support document for amendments not encompassed
rubrics_metrics.description: For any amendment to the claims (including any new claim) that is not encompassed by the accelerated examination support document, applicant is required to provide an updated accelerated examination support document that encompasses the amended/new claims at the time of filing the amendment. Failure to provide such updated document will cause the amendment to be treated as not fully responsive and not entered. Any IDS filed with an updated support document must comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: updated support document must accompany the amendment; do not file late.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement for replies and consequence of paper filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply or other papers must be filed electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system so that papers will be expeditiously processed and considered. If papers are not filed electronically or the reply is not fully responsive, the final disposition of the application may occur later than twelve months from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS filing is mandatory for timely accelerated processing — paper filings risk losing the 12‑month target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑allowance obligations and timing for issue fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing of a notice of allowance is the final disposition for purposes of the twelve‑month goal. In response to a notice of allowance, applicant must pay the issue fee within three months from the date of mailing of the Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due (form PTOL‑85) to avoid abandonment. To have the application issued expeditiously, applicant must (A) pay the issue fee (and any outstanding fees) within one month from the PTOL‑85 mailing date, and (B) not file any post‑allowance papers not required by the USPTO (e.g., an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 not requested by the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment of issue fee is essential; filing unnecessary post‑allowance papers can delay issuance and jeopardize the accelerated timeline.
